# DUOT: Data center power demand creates a second revenue channel through mobile gas turbine fleet management.

## Bear case first
Why this name fails. A disconfirming reading is that the gas turbine work is an asset-management relationship, not a product sale with a visible backlog; the filing does not quantify fleet revenue or margins [4]. Insider open-market activity is zero over the trailing 12 months (Form 4). Customer evidence is thin: named counterparties are contract entities, and federal award dollars are $2.56M from one DOT contract (USASpending). The company has about 0.6 quarters of cash runway and a shelf on file, so dilution is a near-term risk (Reality check).

## Business today
The company designs, develops, deploys, and operates intelligent technology solutions, including edge data centers and power and energy consulting [0]. It sells hosting, colocation, and managed infrastructure services through edge data centers [7] and infrastructure-related services for data center deployments [14]. For the year ended 2025-12-31, revenue was $27.0M; cash at that date was $1.9M (SEC XBRL).

## Chain position
DUOT occupies the on-site gas generation beneficiary node of the data center power adoption chain. The filing states the company has engaged with third parties for consulting and asset management for power solutions for large data centers supporting AI hyperscalers [3]. The economic logic is that data center operators facing grid interconnection delays may accept a premium for on-site generation; DUOT manages a mobile gas turbine fleet under contract [4].

## Customer graph
Fortress, New APR, and Sawgrass are named enterprise counterparties (Customer graph); Fortress paid a $5.0M cash advance recognized as revenue in 2025 [17]. The 10-Q refers to the fleet asset counterparty as New APR in one note [17] and Sawgrass in another [18] without explaining the relationship. The only government buyer is the Department of Transportation at $2.56M (USASpending). One other filer names the company (Customer graph). Customer evidence is thin; end-customer payments for the gas turbine fleet are not disclosed.

## Insider and management signal
No insider open-market buying or selling appeared in the trailing 12 months (Form 4). Management formed a subsidiary for infrastructure services [5] and signed the Fortress fleet contract [17], but the filing does not state quantified targets or committed capex. The signal is neutral: specific operations, no insider stake change.

## Street view
Sell-side coverage is absent: analyst count, consensus, and mean target are all unavailable (Street view). Thin coverage is part of the setup for an under-covered small cap, but it also means no external validation of the thesis.

## Non-linear case
If the Fortress fleet management contract expands from consulting and operations into a large managed fleet, revenue could scale beyond the current $27.0M base (SEC XBRL). The filing describes demand for power solutions for large data centers and AI hyperscalers [3] and DUOT provides management, sales, and operations for mobile gas turbines [4]. For that outcome, data center interconnection delays must persist, Fortress must deploy additional capital, and DUOT must convert this contract into a recurring asset-management business. The current filing evidence does not show that conversion.

## Evidence
- [0] The Company designs, develops, deploys, and operates intelligent technology solutions, including edge data centers and power and energy consulting.
- [3] The Company has engaged with third parties for consulting and asset management for power solutions for large data centers supporting AI hyperscalers.
- [4] Duos Energy manages deployment and operations of a fleet of mobile gas turbines and balance-of-plant inventory under the AMA.
- [5] In 2026, the Company formed Duos Technology Solutions to provide infrastructure-related services for data center projects.
- [7] The edge data center platform is designed to generate recurring revenues through hosting, colocation, and managed infrastructure services.
- [14] Technology Solutions provides infrastructure-related services for digital infrastructure and data center deployments.
- [17] In December 2024, the Company entered contracts with Fortress to deploy and operate a fleet of mobile gas turbines; the schedule shows a $5.0M cash advance recognized as revenue in 2025.
- [18] In December 2024, the Company entered contracts with Fortress under which it will provide management, sales, and operations functions to Sawgrass in connection with the assets.

## Sizing and survivability
At $10.47M average daily dollar volume, a small fund can size a position but needs about 24 trading days to build it (Reality check). Net cash is $1.9M and cash runway is about 0.6 quarters, so the company likely needs to raise capital. Share count is up 62.1% in 12 months and a shelf is on file; dilution risk threatens the thesis (Reality check).

## What would change our mind
- A 10-K or 10-Q disclosing a named end-customer and quantified backlog for the gas turbine fleet.
- A Form 4 showing insider open-market purchases.
- A new federal award from DOE or DoD for on-site power or data center infrastructure (USASpending).

# SMXT: BESS EPC contractor positioned in the US grid and storage capex cycle

## Bear case first

Revenue is concentrated in one customer. In 2025, $60.2M of EPC revenue came from the Longfellow contract [7], and the other three EPC agreements were signed on Dec 31, 2025 [8][14]. The customer graph shows four named customers and zero other filers naming the company (customer graph). No insider bought or sold in the trailing 12 months (Form 4), and federal awards are $0 (USASpending). The filings do not show project completion dates, backlog totals, or EPC gross margin, so the follow-on thesis is unproven.

## Business today

SolarMax sells engineering, procurement, and construction services for large-scale BESS systems, and it also runs residential and commercial solar installation through subsidiary SREP [11][5]. Since Q3 2025, its primary business has been negotiating and performing EPC services for BESS systems [5]. Total revenue was $91.0M and cash was $8.0M as of 2025-12-31 (SEC XBRL); EPC revenue from the Longfellow contract was $60.2M in 2025 [7].

## Chain position

SolarMax is the EPC contractor node in the US solar and storage adoption chain. It performs construction services for large-scale BESS projects [6][8]. The economic logic is that EPC firms capture a meaningful share of project spend through fixed-price and cost-plus contracts, and multi-year construction timelines create backlog visibility.

## Customer graph

Buyers are four named enterprises: Longfellow BESS I, LLC, Naguabo BESS, LLC, Yabucoa BESS, LLC, and Navboot Holdco, LLC (customer graph). Federal awards are $0 (USASpending). No other filers name the company (customer graph). Customer evidence is thin: all disclosed EPC revenue so far is from the Longfellow contract [7], and the other three contracts are dated Dec 31, 2025 [8].

## Insider and management signal

Form 4 shows net open-market activity of $0, with 0 buys and 0 sales by 0 insiders in the trailing 12 months (Form 4). Management states that services on the first large-scale energy storage initiative commenced in Q3 2025 [0] and that Q1 performance reflects continued execution [1]. No quantified financial targets are in the excerpts.

## Street view

Sell-side aggregators show no coverage: unknown analyst count, consensus n/a, and mean target n/a (Street view). No firm rating actions are in the provided facts. For an under-covered small cap, thin coverage is part of the setup.

## Non-linear case

The three Dec 31, 2025 BESS contracts [8][14], if executed, can grow revenue from the current $60.2M EPC base [7] against a projected $125B US solar market [4]. The company has prior EPC experience from Chinese solar farms [9] and states it is expanding US commercial and industrial services [3]. For the non-linear outcome, new customers must appear beyond the four named entities, and future 10-Q and 10-K filings must show revenue from the Puerto Rico and Corpus Christi projects. The path to a multiple of today's business depends on customer diversification and execution margins.

## Evidence

- CEO described the Q3 2025 start on the first large-scale storage initiative and continued Q1 execution [0][1].
- Management is pursuing commercial solar development, industrial EPC, LED lighting, and residential expansion [3].
- The US solar market is expected to exceed $125B by 2030 [4].
- Since Q3 2025, the primary business has been EPC services for solar-based BESS systems [5].
- EPC services commenced on a 430 MWh Texas BESS under the Longfellow agreement [6].
- EPC revenue from the Longfellow contract was $60.2M in 2025 [7].
- On Dec 31, 2025, SolarMax entered three EPC agreements for BESS systems in Puerto Rico and Corpus Christi [8].
- From 2015 through 2021, most China revenue came from EPC contracts for large solar farms [9].
- SREP is the US subsidiary that performs the four commercial EPC agreements [11].
- The Longfellow agreement was dated July 31, 2025 [13].
- SolarMax entered four BESS EPC contracts in 2025 [19].
- Naguabo is in Ceiba Municipality, Puerto Rico; Yabucoa is in Humacao Municipality, Puerto Rico; Navboot is in Corpus Christi, Texas [15][16][17].

## Sizing and survivability

A small fund would face real liquidity limits: average daily dollar volume is $451.0K and building a position would take about 544 trading days (reality check). Cash is $8.0M (SEC XBRL), but the provided facts do not disclose burn, so runway is not calculable. Share count rose 24.2% in 12 months (reality check), making dilution a live threat to the thesis.

## What would change our mind

A Form 4 showing insider open-market purchases would change the read on conviction. A 10-Q or 10-K reporting revenue from Naguabo, Yabucoa, or Navboot would confirm that the Dec 31 contracts are converting. A USASpending federal award or an 8-K naming a new customer would broaden the customer graph.

# SLNH: Behind-the-meter renewable data center capacity, with the 300 MW HPC project as the unproven upside

## Bear case first
The disconfirming read is that Soluna is not in the mapped node; it operates behind-the-meter data centers [8]. The theme does not create a new business for Soluna; the HPC expansion is a data center business, not a customer-funded C&I energy project. Customer evidence is thin: no named enterprise customer appears in the excerpts (Customer graph), and federal awarded dollars total $14.45K (USASpending). Insiders sold a net $649.2K over 12 months (Form 4). At $462K cash and negative net cash, equity issuance may be needed before Project Kati 2 revenue (SEC XBRL, Reality check).

## Business today
Soluna develops digital infrastructure co-located with renewable plants, including wind, solar, or hydro [2][3]. It uses two data center designs: modular for Bitcoin and AI-ready for HPC [5][6][7]. Revenue sources are proprietary Bitcoin mining, third-party Bitcoin hosting, and demand response, with HPC leasing under development [12][13][14][15]. As of 2025-12-31, revenue was $29.7M and cash was $462K (SEC XBRL).

## Chain position
Soluna maps to the behind-the-meter node, order 2 beneficiary. Data centers draw directly from co-located plants and existing interconnection [8][11], converting underutilized energy into computing capacity [4]. It is an indirect beneficiary of rising grid costs, not a C&I solar or storage provider.

## Customer graph
The customer-validation subscore is 4/5, but the graph is thin. Named enterprise customers: none in the excerpts (Customer graph). Government: $14.45K in federal awards, with $10.69K from the Department of Veterans Affairs and $3.76K from the Department of Defense (USASpending). Unproven: Project Kati 2 tenants; HPC initially targets hyperscalers, neoclouds, and later enterprise customers [19]. One other filer names Soluna (Customer graph).

## Insider and management signal
Net open-market insider activity was -$649.2K over 3 buys and 30 sales by 1 insider (Form 4). The sales dominate. Management gives specific targets: more than 300 MW with Metrobloks [14] and Dorothy 3 positioned across from the Briscoe substation [1]. The insider signal tempers that conviction.

## Street view
Street coverage is thin: unknown analyst count, consensus n/a, target n/a (Street view). No firm rating actions are available. Thin coverage is part of the setup.

## Non-linear case
Project Kati 2 is the non-linear path: more than 300 MW for AI and HPC customers [14]. Soluna closed on 397 acres [0], and Dorothy 3 sits across from the Briscoe substation [1]. If renewable behind-the-meter capacity becomes scarce, this project could reduce Bitcoin's weight in revenue [12][13]. Financing and named tenants are not yet in the evidence.

## Evidence
- Closed purchase of 397 acres in Briscoe County, Texas [0]; Dorothy 3 is positioned for direct behind-the-meter access to owned generation [1].
- Data centers are co-located with wind, solar, or hydro [2]; Soluna owns and operates digital infrastructure for energy-intensive computing [3].
- It seeks to convert underutilized energy into computing capacity [4].
- Two designs exist: modular for Bitcoin [5][6], AI-ready for HPC [7].
- Data centers operate behind-the-meter and use existing interconnection [8][11].
- Revenue sources: proprietary Bitcoin mining [12], third-party hosting [13], HPC [14], demand response [15].
- Project Kati 2 is being engineered for more than 300 MW in partnership with Metrobloks [14].
- HPC initially targets hyperscalers, neoclouds, and later enterprise customers [19].

## Sizing and survivability
At $22.2M average daily dollar volume, a small fund can build in about 12 days (Reality check). Cash runway is about 0.2 quarters, net cash is -$17.4M, share count rose 711.4%, and a shelf is on file (Reality check, SEC XBRL). These facts threaten the thesis.

## What would change our mind
- An 8-K or 10-K names a tenant or executed lease for Project Kati 2.
- Form 4s show net open-market insider buying over six months.
- USASpending shows a federal award above $14.45K, or a filing discloses a utility or government demand response contract.

# NNBR: Retooling auto capacity into the electrical grid capex supercycle

## Bear case first
The grid thesis rests on a presentation target, not on orders. Current revenue is high-volume auto, HVAC, and diesel components (1); management says it will wean the lower-margin legacy auto business as contracts expire (0). The Electrical Grid & Data Center plan has no named customers, no federal awards (USASpending), and no dated milestones; the only timeline is a 2029-2030 sales goal (0). Insiders sold $45.3K and bought nothing (Form 4); the share count is up 64.2% with a shelf on file (reality check).

## Business today
NN manufactures high-volume precision components for power steering, braking, transmissions, gasoline fuel systems, HVAC, and diesel systems (1). Revenue was $422.2M and cash was $11.4M as of 2025-12-31 (SEC XBRL). Management is retooling equipment toward Electrical Grid & Data Center, Defense & Electronics, Medical, and High-Value Vehicle (0).

## Chain position
The mapped position is first-order: a component supplier into high-voltage transformer, switchgear, and circuit breaker manufacturers. Utility procurement for data center load pushes backlogs past two years, which firms pricing and flows volume to suppliers. NN's current grid revenue is not disclosed; its place in the chain rests on the stated growth plan (0), not on confirmed backlog.

## Customer graph
Government buyers: $0 in federal awards (USASpending). Enterprise buyers: none named; 3 other filers name the company, but no purchasing relationship is identified. The grid plan is unproven at the customer level; legacy customers are described only by application (1). Customer evidence is thin.

## Insider and management signal
Net open-market insider activity is $-45.3K from 1 sale and 0 buys (Form 4). Management language is quantified: $80M to $100M of new business growth per year, a $422M to $600M sales goal, and explicit equipment retooling (0). The signals conflict: no insider buying, committed targets.

## Street view
Sell-side coverage is unknown: analyst count, consensus, and mean target are n/a, and no firm rating actions are visible. Thin coverage is part of the set-up but means no independent validation of the plan.

## Non-linear case
The path to a multiple of today's market cap is a margin mix shift: grid and data center components at higher margins replacing the legacy auto book, with revenue reaching the $600M target (0). That requires NN to convert retooled capacity into purchase orders from transformer or switchgear OEMs and to sustain $80M to $100M of new business growth per year (0). Pricing power is the non-linear element; long lead times let suppliers push price rather than accept auto-like terms. The $301M market cap (reality check) embeds none of the transition beyond the investor presentation (0).

## Evidence
- Management plans to add $80M to $100M of new business growth per year, wean lower-margin legacy auto, and retool equipment (0).
- Long-term goal: $422M sales in 2025 to $600M by 2029-2030 (0).
- Growth areas named: Electrical Grid & Data Center, Defense & Electronics, Medical, High-Value Vehicle (0).
- Current business: high-volume components for power steering, braking, transmissions, gasoline fuel systems, HVAC, diesel injection, and diesel emissions (1).

## Sizing and survivability
Average daily dollar volume is $13.2M, so a small fund needs 19 trading days to build a position (reality check). Cash is $11.4M against net cash of -$145.7M (SEC XBRL; reality check), and the share count is up 64.2% with a shelf on file (reality check). Dilution risk is material; the negative net cash position is the key survivability constraint.

## What would change our mind
- An open-market insider buy on a Form 4 would reverse the selling signal.
- A federal award from DOE or DoD visible in USASpending would add a government customer.
- A 10-Q or 10-K with a named grid customer or quantified backlog would move the thesis from presentation to proof.

# ESP: A small grid-equipment supplier positioned for US substation spending only if utility orders appear

## Bear case first

The filing evidence is a static product list, not a growth plan. ESP already sells power transformers and power distribution equipment, but the filing does not quantify backlog, capacity, named customers, or any committed capital spending. The street and customer evidence is thin, and management language contains no strategic commitment beyond routine enumeration. The dossier shows net open-market insider selling of -$1.723M over the trailing 12 months (Form 4), while share count rose 7.1% (SEC XBRL). The strongest disconfirming read is that this is a small, dilutive, insider-sold name with no evidence of new orders, and the grid capex theme simply describes existing products that are not yet confirmed to be in demand.

## Business today

ESP’s primary products are power supplies, power converters, filters, power transformers, magnetic components, power distribution equipment, UPS systems, and antennas [0]. Revenue was $9.596M and cash was $18.863M as of 2025-06-30 (SEC XBRL). The filing identifies no customer segments or end-markets.

## Chain position

ESP occupies the grid equipment supply node for power transformers and power distribution equipment. These products sit directly in the utility procurement chain for substations and transmission lines, making ESP a first-order beneficiary if US grid capex accelerates. Long lead times and tight supplier capacity would allow pricing to firm, but ESP-specific backlog is not evidenced.

## Customer graph

Federal awards total $18.678M, including Department of Defense awards of $10.129M, $1.734M, and $1.295M (USASpending). One other filer names ESP in its own filing. No named enterprise customers appear in the excerpts, so enterprise demand is unproven and government awards appear to be the main visible source of revenue.

## Insider and management signal

Trailing 12 months Form 4 shows 0 open-market buys and 134 open-market sales, net -$1.723M (Form 4). Management language in the filing is a generic product list with no named programs, capex targets, or quantified commitments [0]. Insider selling is a negative conviction signal, and the filing does not offset it with management action.

## Street view

Sell-side aggregator data show unknown analyst count, consensus n/a, and mean target n/a (Street view). There is no rated firm or visible rating action. For an under-covered small-cap, this coverage gap means the market is not pricing in a grid capex story until direct evidence emerges.

## Non-linear case

If utility procurement pushes transformer and distribution equipment backlogs to multi-year levels, even a small supplier can gain pricing power on a small revenue base. ESP’s revenue is only $9.596M, so one or two large contracts could be material (SEC XBRL). The non-linear path requires ESP to convert the general grid shortage into named orders and then add capacity to deliver them. The filing [0] does not show that any such programs exist yet, so the path is conditional on future evidence.

## Evidence

- Primary products include power transformers and power distribution equipment [0].
- The filing describes existing product lines without named orders, capacity additions, or strategic targets [0].

## Sizing and survivability

Average daily dollar volume is $2.944M, implying roughly 84 trading days to build a position (price data). Net cash is $18.863M against revenue of $9.596M, so cash runway is not an immediate constraint (SEC XBRL). Share count rose 7.1% in 12 months, and that dilution risk is a real threat given the company’s small equity base (SEC XBRL).

## What would change our mind

A 10-Q, 10-K, or 8-K that discloses backlog, a named utility customer, or transformer capacity expansion would be direct support for the thesis. Open-market Form 4 buys by insiders would reverse the current negative insider signal. A new federal award or customer contract naming ESP as supplier would also strengthen the customer evidence.

# NEXT: Grid capex supercycle has no filing support in an LNG EPC change-order file

## Bear case first
Every cited filing is a change order under the Rio Grande LNG fixed price turnkey EPC agreement, not a transmission or substation contract. The evidence contains no mention of grid, data center load, or utility customers, so the grid capex thesis has no confirmation in the primary record. The company has $0M revenue, net cash of -$8,683.6M, and roughly 3.4 quarters of cash runway (reality check), so survivability dominates before any thematic upside. The $6.95M insider buying (Form 4) is the only positive signal but does not bridge the gap to the grid map position.

## Business today
The cited exhibits to NEXT's 10-Q document change orders for the Rio Grande Natural Gas Liquefaction Facility, naming owner Rio Grande LNG, LLC and contractor Bechtel Energy Inc. under the September 14, 2022 fixed price turnkey EPC agreement [0]. The changes cover compressor installation [1], trench design revisions [2], commodity price adjustments [3], tariff reimbursements [5], and scrubber installation [6]. Revenue is $0M and cash is $143.8M as of 2025-12-31 (SEC XBRL).

## Chain position
The map position is transmission and substation EPC contractors that book utility grid awards. NEXT, on the filing evidence, is the owner side of an LNG EPC contract, not a contractor that books grid capex [0]. The labor-scarcity and backlog logic for transmission does not apply to a company with only LNG change orders on file [1][2][6].

## Customer graph
No named enterprise customers and $0M in federal awards are in the data (USASpending). Five other SEC filers name the company (SEC XBRL), but the cited evidence names only EPC counterparties Rio Grande LNG, LLC and Bechtel Energy Inc. [0]. The paying customer for LNG output is unproven.

## Insider and management signal
Four insiders bought a net $6.95M on the open market with zero sales over the trailing 12 months, a conviction signal (Form 4). Management language is change order boilerplate, including no-impact confirmations on guarantees [9], with no grid or data center discussion. The insider signal is real but disconnected from the mapped catalyst.

## Street view
Coverage is unknown: consensus and mean target are n/a, and no firm rating actions are visible because bank reports are paywalled. Thin coverage at a $1,956M market cap means the grid theme is not yet debated by the street.

## Non-linear case
A multiple of today's business would require NEXT to convert its LNG EPC relationship into transmission or substation work, which no filing supports. Completion of Rio Grande LNG could re-rate the stock, but that is an LNG thesis, not a grid thesis. The non-linear path is speculative until a filing names a grid-related contract or customer.

## Evidence
- EPC change order header for Rio Grande LNG, owner Rio Grande LNG, LLC, contractor Bechtel Energy Inc., effective April 27, 2026 [0].
- Workshop air compressor procurement, installation, and commissioning [1].
- Tug berth utility trench location design change [2].
- Q1-2026 commodity index value updates under Attachment KK [3].
- Change order signed May 4, 2026 for February 2026 TRA updates on new covered items [4][5].
- Fuel gas scrubber and Coriolis meter installation [6].
- Change order signed June 5, 2026, effective June 19, 2026 [7].
- Previously executed change orders incorporated into Attachment C [8].
- No impact on acceptance criteria, performance guarantees, or basis of design [9].

## Sizing and survivability
Average daily dollar volume of $20.5M implies about 12 trading days to build a position (reality check). Net cash is -$8,683.6M, runway is about 3.4 quarters, and the share count is up 2% in 12 months (reality check). A small fund can build a position, but the funding gap and dilution risk threaten the thesis before any grid exposure appears.

## What would change our mind
A 10-Q or 10-K naming a transmission, substation, or data center interconnection contract. A Form 4 showing net insider selling, contradicting the current buy signal. A federal award or named enterprise customer tied to grid engineering in USASpending or XBRL data.

# BV: No data center gas generation aftermarket exposure; thesis fails on filing evidence

## Bear case first
A disconfirming reading of the evidence is that BrightView is a landscape maintenance and development contractor. Every revenue line in the quarterly filing comes from Maintenance Services or Development Services, with no mention of gas turbines, engine aftermarket, or data center load [0][2][7]. The dossier shows no insider buying, only $273.95K in federal awards, and negative net cash. The filing cannot support a claim that the US grid capex supercycle benefits this company.

## Business today
BrightView sells recurring landscape maintenance, snow removal, and development services to Fortune 500 corporate campuses, HOAs, public parks, airports, municipalities, hospitals, schools, restaurants, retail, and golf courses [2][16]. The 10-Q reports net service revenues of $717.6M for the three months ended June 30, 2026 [7]. The dossier lists no XBRL revenue as of 2025-09-30 and reports cash of $74.5M (SEC XBRL).

## Chain position
BrightView occupies no node in the data center gas generation adoption chain. The thesis expected gas turbine and engine service and aftermarket providers, but the filing describes only landscape maintenance and development services [0][2][13]. No economic logic connects route-based landscape services to turbine overhaul.

## Customer graph
Enterprise: no named customers appear in the excerpts. Government: federal awards total $273.95K, including $106.94K from the Department of Defense, $29.98K from the Department of Veterans Affairs, and $26.33K from the Department of Justice (USASpending). Unproven: no data center or generation customer is identified. Seven other filers name BrightView. Customer evidence for the thesis is thin.

## Insider and management signal
Form 4 shows net open-market activity of $0 across 0 buys and 0 sales by 0 insiders over the trailing 12 months (Form 4). Management language focuses on seasonality, recurring contracts, and service delivery [3][19]. There is no management commitment to the data center or gas generation theme.

## Street view
Sell-side aggregators show unknown analyst count, consensus n/a, and mean target n/a (Street view). No recent firm rating actions are visible; bank reports are paywalled. Thin coverage does not create a hidden setup because the filing evidence contradicts the thesis.

## Non-linear case
A non-linear outcome would require BrightView to transform into a gas generation services provider. That would appear as new reportable segments, named contracts, or related revenue in 10-K or 10-Q filings, none of which are present [0][7][13]. Without that evidence, a path to a multiple of today's business is not supported.

## Evidence
- BrightView is aligned into two reportable segments: Maintenance Services and Development Services [0].
- Revenue is generated from Maintenance Services and Development Services [1].
- Maintenance Services revenues are generated through landscape maintenance and snow removal [2].
- Recurring landscape maintenance contracts run one to three years and are generally cancellable with 30-90 days notice [3].
- Net service revenues were $717.6M for the three months ended June 30, 2026 [7].
- Maintenance Services primarily consists of recurring landscape maintenance, snow removal, and enhancements [11].
- Customers include Fortune 500 corporate campuses, HOAs, public parks, airports, municipalities, hospitals, schools, restaurants, retail, and golf courses [16].
- Seasonality affects the business, including spring planting, fall leaf removal, winter snow, and summer mowing [19].

## Sizing and survivability
Average daily dollar volume is $12.39M, so a position takes about 20 trading days to build (Reality check). Net cash is -$715.7M and cash is $74.5M (SEC XBRL). Share count is down 2.4% in 12 months, so there is no trailing dilution; no shelf is cited in the dossier facts (Reality check). Negative net cash and the absence of thematic revenue threaten the thesis.

## What would change our mind
A 10-K or 10-Q segment disclosure showing gas turbine maintenance or data center power generation revenue. A Form 4 open-market insider purchase. A federal award identifying BrightView as a turbine or generation service provider.

# GSAT: Satellite IoT operator with no grid or data center exposure, thin customer evidence, and heavy insider selling

## Bear case first

GSAT's existing satellite MSS and IoT services [2] produced $273.0M in revenue, and the company holds $447.5M cash (SEC XBRL), so the data center interconnection theme is not needed to keep it solvent. Federal awards, while small at $1.9M (USASpending), confirm government buyers. A short also faces $99.1M average daily dollar volume (reality check), which can squeeze. Yet insiders sold $30.0M with zero buys (Form 4), no named enterprise customer appears in the excerpts, and the filings contain no data center or grid interconnection program, capex, or revenue line. The $1.1B market cap therefore rests on a theme the filings never mention.

## Business today

Globalstar sells Commercial IoT, SPOT, and Duplex MSS services [2], plus connectivity for areas not served by terrestrial networks [1]. Revenue is $273.0M and cash is $447.5M (SEC XBRL); net cash is negative at $36.3M, implying debt of about $483.8M (reality check).

## Chain position

The map positions this name at an at-risk node: data center developers awaiting grid interconnection. GSAT does not occupy that node on the evidence in the filings, which describe satellite IoT and MSS services [2] and terrestrial backup use cases [1]. No filing link connects its revenue to data center load, grid study capacity, or network upgrade fees.

## Customer graph

Government agencies pay GSAT: $538.8K from DOJ, $175.2K from DoD, and $158.7K from DHS, totaling $1.9M (USASpending). No named enterprise customer appears in the excerpts. Four other SEC filers name GSAT (customer graph), but the filings do not quantify commercial revenue from them. Customer evidence is thin against $273.0M revenue (SEC XBRL).

## Insider and management signal

Insiders sold $30.0M net with zero buys and 50 sales over the trailing 12 months (Form 4). Management language in the 10-K is descriptive: satellite IoT demand is growing [3], LEO systems have a latency advantage [4], but no data center or grid program, capex target, or quantified goal appears. The sale cluster reads as low conviction.

## Street view
